newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- munis end down 3/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- munis end down 3/8.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended down 3/8 of a point Wednesday as the threat of higher oil prices and talk of a large 10-year note seller wrought sharper losses in U.S. Treasuries, market sources said.
"This is much weaker here this afternoon," a municipal trader said. "I would say in the last two hours, maybe last three hours it's down an O4 (four basis points)."
The trader cited the Tampa Sports Authority, Fla., 5-1/4s of 2027, which recently were freed to trade. The bonds came at a 5.56 percent yield originally.
"Right now the market is 5.59 to 5.58," the trader said.
The trader attributed muni's fall to government market weakness.
"That's all it is, no doubt about it," he said. "We are lagging them on the downside, but we are starting to catch up right now."

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond ended down 19/32 at 98-17/32 to yield 6.74 percent. In debt futures, the September municipal contract closed down 6/32 at 117-6/32. The September T-bond contract closed down 2/32 at 111-23/32. The MOB spread was 175 ticks.

Tony Crescenzi, chief bond market strategist at Miller Tabak Hirsch & Co, said what looks like a "strong commitment from OPEC to curtail their chronic over production" factored in Treasuries' decline.

"The move lower in oil from over $26 a barrel to about $19 a barrel had helped the market throughout the year," Crescenzi said, adding that the move translated to bond friendly news on producer and consumer prices.

Crescenzi also cited a seller of more than $1 billion of 10-year Treasuries, as well as some hedge fund selling. The New Jersey Economic Development Authority's $2.8 billion offering also had an impact on governments, he said.

"One dealer said to me that they were seeing people swapping out of Treasuries to go into that New Jersey (deal)," Crescenzi said. "It was the biggest muni deal in history for long-dated paper, and they were selling strips apparently."
He added, however, that the deal appeared to be well received.
"It's not like dealers had to hedge for it because it was very well subscribed, well sponsored," Crescenzi said.

Elsewhere in new issues, Bear Stearns & Co said it repriced $100 million Florida Housing Finance Agency bonds, adjusting yields in several maturities but leaving the top tax-exempt yield in 2029 unchanged at 5.90 percent.
Merrill Lynch & Co repriced $95 million Wisconsin Housing and Economic Development Authority bonds at a top tax exempt yield of 6.0 percent in 2028.
On the competitive side, Smith Barney Inc won $69 million New York State Environmental Facilities Corp at a 5.08 percent true interest cost.
BancAmerica Securities said it won $47 million San Francisco general obligation bonds at a true interest cost of 5.06 percent.
